description: A four-string tanpura drone: each strum plucks the next string in turn, and a bridge control sets how much the strings buzz

params.text: Sets the shape of the bridge the strings rest on, a plain string tone at CLOSED and a buzzing one at OPEN
Transposes all four strings by 0 to 11 semitones
Transposes all four strings by 0 to 2 octaves
Sets the note the first string is tuned to, named in the Indian sargam from Sa to Ni; the other three stay on the root
Plucks the next string in the cycle each time it is pressed
Puts the cycle back to the start, so the next strum plucks the first string

inputs.text: Plucks the next string in the cycle on each rising edge past 2V
Adds to the bridge slider, 1V covering the whole of its travel, and the lamp on the slider shows the total
A rising edge past 2V puts the cycle back to the start, so the next strum plucks the first string
Transposes all four strings, a volt per octave rounded down to a semitone, and only between -1V and +2V
Transposes the first string on its own, a volt per octave rounded down to a semitone, and only between -1V and +2V

notes: nothing sounds until a clock is patched to STRUM or the strum button is pressed
both pitch jacks are read only at the moment a string is plucked, so a change of voltage is heard on the next strum rather than at once
the maker suggests strumming slowly, around 60 BPM, for the sound of a real tanpura

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
0 to 1V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
